archetypes.name: warn-propagation-architecture
archetypes.rationale: All three refactored sites omit WARN from the --allow list for read-result-env.sh, leaving it unclear whether route/review/publish driver warnings reach the operator; the Step 5d prose-level replay contract assumes WARN values are accessible but no fence mechanism loads them.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine how WARN= lines emitted by design-route.sh, run-step3-review.sh, and design-publish.sh surface to the operator after the refactor. In skills/design/SKILL.md Step 0b, WARN is absent from the --allow list for read-result-env.sh and no replay loop follows the source; in Step 5c, WARN is also absent and the Step 5d 'Driver WARN replay (top chat)' prose relies on already-deleted files. Determine whether read-result-env.sh itself emits WARN lines as side-channel stdout (so they'd appear inline without being sourced), or whether they are silently dropped at each of the three sites. Also assess whether the responsibility split — merge_router_flags() now in design-route.sh owning the Brainstorm title-prefix auto-enable, while the orchestrator still reads BRAINSTORM_PREFIX from the safe env and re-sets brainstorm_requested — creates a double-update path that could misfire when BRAINSTORM_PREFIX is true in the result env but was set by prior design-route logic rather than the current invocation. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: behavioral-change-risk
archetypes.rationale: The Step 3 fence now runs the shared reader before the rc=2 abort (loading LOOP_STATUS before returning 2), PLAN_REVIEW_CONTINUE_REASON is removed from the narrow stdout overlay and may be stdout-only in run-step3-review.sh, and the release SKILL.md rebase sync step maps exit codes against rebase-push.sh without contract verification.
archetypes.prompt_body: In skills/design/scripts/test-step3-orchestrator-fence.sh, apply_step3_handoff now invokes read-result-env.sh and the narrow stdout overlay before checking plan_review_rc=2; confirm whether any caller of apply_step3_handoff inspects LOOP_STATUS or other sourced variables on the rc=2 code path and whether loading them before the early-return is safe or surprising. Separately, verify that run-step3-review.sh writes PLAN_REVIEW_CONTINUE_REASON to .step3-review-result.env (making it readable by the shared reader) rather than emitting it only to stdout; the narrow overlay in SKILL.md covers only STEP3_REVIEW_LOOP_STATUS/POSTPLAN_RC/DEDUP_RC/FINAL_ROUND_NUM/WARN, so a stdout-only emission would silently drop the key. Also review the new .claude/skills/release/SKILL.md Step 1 rebase sync block: confirm that rebase-push.sh's actual exit-code contract matches the diff's mapping (0=fresh-or-synced, 1=conflicts, other=network/git failure), and check whether running a rebase on main during --dry-run could leave a dirty working tree that breaks the subsequent dirty-tree guard. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
